explanation:
## What the grids are made of

Every grid is dense, colourful noise in colours 0, 2, 3, 4 and 7. Each grid also holds exactly one small shape drawn in colour **8**: a plus in pairs 1 and 3, a T in pair 4, and a 4-cell zig-zag in pair 2. That 8-shape is the only thing that stands out, so it is the natural thing to call a **template**.

## What changes

The fact sheet shows that every changed cell goes **3 → 8**, and nothing else ever changes. So the output finds places where the template's shape is "hidden" in the colour-3 noise and paints them 8.

- **Pair 4:** the template is a T (`888 / .8. / .8.`). One occurrence is turned 8: cells (4,8), (5,8..10), (6,8). That is the same T rotated by 90°.
- **Pair 2:** the template is `8.8 / .88`. Two occurrences are turned 8. The one at rows 2–3 has the same orientation. The pair at rows 11–13 (cells (11,10), (12,9), (13,9), (13,10)) uses a rotated or mirrored version.
- **Pairs 1 and 3:** pluses of colour 3 become pluses of 8.

**Matching is not "whole component equals template."** In pair 1, the green blob at bbox [9,10,11,11] has 5 cells. Only the 4 cells forming the template shape turn 8, and the extra green neighbour stays 3. So an occurrence is any placement of the template, in any of its 8 rotations or reflections, where every template cell is 3. Neighbouring 3s don't matter.

**Overlapping placements.** Within a larger green patch, several placements can overlap. The rule I take from the reference is:

1. Choose the largest set of **non-overlapping** placements.
2. On ties, prefer placements that don't need a reflection.

The reference also checks that every tied optimum yields the same set of painted cells. That makes the answer unambiguous rather than dependent on scan order.

## Checking against the demonstrations

| Pair | Copies found and painted | Cells changed (fact sheet) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 pluses × 4 | 8 |
| 2 | 3 zig-zags × 4 | 12 |
| 3 | 2 pluses × 5 | 10 |
| 4 | 1 T × 5 | 5 |

In each pair these are exactly the changed cells in the fact sheet. The colour to search for (3) is the same in every pair, even though the background varies (it is 2 in pair 2 and 3 in the test). So 3 is used as a constant, and the template is always read from the 8 cells.

## The test input

The template is the 8-shape at (4,2), (5,2), (5,3), (6,3), a vertical S/Z zig-zag. Its rotations and reflections are slid over the grid. Every placement lying entirely on 3-cells is a candidate. The largest disjoint set is chosen, preferring unreflected copies on ties, and those cells are painted 8.

Each accepted copy is one teaching stage, emitted as it is painted, followed by a final summary emit.
